name: Ceramic 70
shortDescription: Huper Optik Ceramic 70 delivers near-clear solar control with 70% VLT, 99% UV block, and signal-safe TiN ceramic construction for Philadelphia offices and rowhomes.
description:
Ceramic 70 sits at the bright end of Huper Optik's flagship Ceramic Series — 70% visible light transmission paired with the patented dual-layer Titanium Nitride (TiN) ceramic coating that earned Huper Optik its US patent. For Philadelphia property owners who want meaningful solar protection without darkening their interiors, Ceramic 70 is the natural starting point.

The TiN ceramic construction is 100% metal-free, which means no interference with Wi-Fi, GPS, cellular signals, or smart-home devices — a practical differentiator for Center City offices, University City research buildings, and Fishtown rowhomes with modern home automation. The film rejects 83% of infrared radiation and blocks 99% of UV rays while maintaining a neutral, low-reflective appearance.

For Philadelphia rowhomes with south or east-facing single-pane glass, Ceramic 70 addresses UV-driven fading and summer heat gain without creating the dimmed, cave-like effect that darker films can produce in narrower row house rooms. Historic district properties with glass restrictions often find Ceramic 70 fits within HOA or preservation guidelines because it reads as nearly clear from the exterior.

Window Film Philadelphia evaluates Ceramic 70 suitability against glass type, orientation, existing coatings, and frame condition. Ceramic 70 carries Huper Optik's lifetime residential warranty and 15-year commercial coverage.

name: Ceramic 50

description:
Ceramic 50 lands in the middle of Huper Optik's Ceramic Series — 50% visible light transmission with the patented dual-layer Titanium Nitride (TiN) coating that defines the line. It is the most versatile specification in the series: bright enough to preserve the feel of open interiors while assertive enough to make a meaningful reduction in solar heat gain and glare.

The 100% metal-free ceramic construction carries 83% infrared rejection and 99% UV block across all Ceramic Series options. For Center City offices with high-volume glazing, Ceramic 50 reduces peak solar load on south and west elevations without requiring a more aggressive VLT that might affect daylight quality or require lighting compensation. In Philadelphia commercial buildings seeking LEED documentation, Ceramic 50's solar heat gain reduction contributes to energy performance credits.

For Philadelphia residential applications — particularly Fishtown townhomes, Rittenhouse condominiums, and Graduate Hospital rowhomes with afternoon west exposure — Ceramic 50 provides a balanced choice that keeps rooms comfortable without the heavy-tinted appearance of darker films. The neutral, low-reflective exterior look is compatible with most HOA and historic district glass guidelines across Philadelphia's preservation zones.

Huper Optik Ceramic 50 carries lifetime residential warranty and 15-year commercial coverage backed by Eastman Chemical Company.

name: Therm-X 70
shortDescription: Huper Optik Therm-X 70 is a low-emissivity insulating film with 70% VLT — engineered for Philadelphia rowhomes with older single-pane glass needing year-round thermal improvement.
description:
Therm-X 70 is the clearest option in Huper Optik's Therm-X Series — a low-emissivity insulating film engineered for year-round thermal performance rather than solar rejection alone. At 70% VLT, Therm-X 70 adds an insulating layer to existing single-pane glass that helps retain heat in winter and reduce solar gain in summer without significantly altering the light levels or exterior appearance of the window.

Philadelphia sits in IECC Climate Zone 4A — a mixed-humid climate with hot summers and cold winters — making it an ideal market for low-E window film. The city's housing stock includes one of the largest concentrations of older single-pane rowhome glass in the Northeast. Therm-X is engineered for this scenario: adding meaningful thermal resistance to existing glass without the cost or disruption of full window replacement.

For Fishtown row houses, South Philly twins, and Mt. Airy craftsman homes with original single-pane wood windows, Therm-X 70 helps address the drafts and heat loss that older glass produces in winter while blocking UV fading and some summer heat gain. At 70% VLT, the film maintains the open, light-filled character of rooms where natural light is a priority — ideal for north-facing rooms or spaces where daylight is limited.

Therm-X 70 carries Huper Optik's lifetime residential warranty.

For Philadelphia property owners who want both the insulating benefits of Therm-X and a modest reduction in glare and solar heat gain during the summer, Therm-X 50 provides a balanced specification. At 52% VLT, it is bright enough for everyday use in living rooms, offices, and commercial spaces while reducing peak summer exposure on east- and south-facing glass.

Historic building preservation often presents constraints on window replacement — the Therm-X Series, applied to the interior surface, can improve thermal performance for Philadelphia historic properties within preservation districts without requiring alterations visible from the exterior. Therm-X 50 carries 99% UV block, which also addresses fading in period interiors where original flooring, millwork, and furnishings need protection.

name: Clear Shield
shortDescription: Huper Optik Clear Shield is a 4-mil clear safety film for Philadelphia glass that retains fragments after impact, delays forced entry, and protects occupants without altering the window's appearance.
description:
Huper Optik Clear Shield is a 4-mil transparent safety and security film designed to hold glass fragments in place after impact. It installs on the interior surface of existing glass — storefront panels, door sidelites, school windows, government building facades, and residential entry points — without changing the look of the window. From outside, treated glass looks identical to untreated glass.

For Philadelphia schools, government buildings, museums along the Benjamin Franklin Parkway, and retail storefronts on high-traffic commercial corridors, Clear Shield provides a passive glass retention layer that works continuously without requiring power, maintenance, or behavioral changes from building occupants. When glass breaks — from a storm, an accident, or attempted forced entry — the film holds the fragments in a coherent pattern that slows penetration and reduces laceration risk.

Philadelphia's retail environment has elevated concerns about smash-and-grab incidents, particularly on high-value commercial corridors. Clear Shield film adds meaningful delay to forced entry through storefront glass — the time required to penetrate film-retained glass versus bare glass is a practical deterrent in scenarios where speed of access is the attacker's primary advantage.

Clear Shield can be layered with Huper Optik solar control or decorative films for a combined security and solar specification. Carries a 10-year commercial warranty.
